cards.text: Jesus is surrounded by a crowd. A BIG one. Then some visitors show up wanting to see Him, and these aren't strangers. They've known Him for years.

cards.question: Who comes to see Jesus while the crowd is packed around Him?
Jesus' mother and brothers make their way through the crowd and walk right up to Him.

cards.text: They can't reach Him. The crowd is too thick. You know that kind of crowd, friend. You say "excuse me" FORTY times and you've moved about three inches.

cards.question: Jesus is told that His mother and brothers are standing ___ wanting to see Him.

cards.text: So the message gets passed to Jesus through all those people, like the world's slowest group chat. Now everybody's waiting to hear what He'll say.

cards.question: Jesus answers. Who does He say His mother and brothers are?

answers.text: Those who hear God's word and carry it out
Those who follow Him from town to town
Those who sit closest to Him and listen

cards.question: According to Jesus, hearing the word of God is enough to be His family, even without carrying it out.

cards.text: Hear it AND carry it out. Back in that junk drawer, I heard somebody say "we really need to clean this drawer" about four hundred times. Friend, NOBODY ever carried it out.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Jesus is surrounded by a crowd." / "A BIG one." / "Then some visitors show up wanting to see Him, and these aren't strangers." / "They've known Him for years." The opening card can have at most three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: This is a recap card. Card 3 has already shown that the family can't walk up to Jesus. Card 4 repeats that ("They can't reach Him. The crowd is too thick.") and adds a joke, but it doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells the next piece of the passage, or this card should be cut.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: This card retells verse 20 after card 5 has already asked about verse 20 and revealed the answer. It tells the baker that the message reached Jesus, which card 5 already showed. It works as a recap, not as the next moment. The setup for card 7 could stand on its own, or this beat could come before card 5.
This last card repeats Jesus' answer from verse 21, which cards 7 and 8 already covered ("Hear it AND carry it out."), and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
